acme-cs: Hey team — running into a puzzling issue on our rerank pipeline. We generate embeddings with emb-large-v2 (dim=1536) but pass them to /v1/rerank using rerank-small-v1. Results are wildly wrong: unrelated docs get top scores. No API error, just bad ordering. Anyone seen this?

alex_support: Sorry you hit this. Can you paste the exact request you're sending to rerank (headers + body, redact keys)? Also which endpoint: are you sending precomputed embeddings or letting the reranker call the embed model?

acme-cs: We send precomputed vectors. Example payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "rerank-small-v1",
  "query": "how to reset session",
  "documents": [
    {"id": "d1", "embedding": [0.003, -0.12, ... 1536 numbers ...]},
    {"id": "d2", "embedding": [0.2, 0.01, ...]}
  ]
}
```
No error response. Server returns scores like 0.98 for clearly unrelated docs.

alex_support: Thanks. Can you also send request logs or X-Request-Id if available? That helps us tie into infra logs.

acme-cs: request-id: req_01GG7YQH2, timestamp 1715004300. Attached are truncated server logs we captured: 
```
[1715004300] rerank-request req_01GG7YQH2: model=rerank-small-v1, precomputed_embeddings=true, incoming_dim=1536
[1715004300] rerank: expected_dim=768, compatibility_mode=auto-pad-truncate
[1715004300] reranker: performing pad/truncate to 768 (mode=truncate)
[1715004300] rerank: compute_scores -> done (sketch approximate), metrics: mean_score=0.67
```

jon-platform: Interesting — logs show the reranker implicitly truncated embedding length instead of failing. That can definitely distort similarity. We had a recent change to default compatibility_mode to "auto-pad-truncate" to avoid breaking customers during model transitions.

kevin-ml: That's the root cause. Rerank-small-v1 expects 768-dim vectors. When precomputed vectors of 1536 are provided we do a naive truncation of the tail which can map unrelated vectors close in L2/cosine space.

kevin-ml: Short repro I ran locally:
```python
# reproduce: emb dim mismatch -> bad scores
query_emb = np.random.randn(1536)
docs = [np.random.randn(1536) for _ in range(50)]
# server truncates
query_trunc = query_emb[:768]
docs_trunc = [d[:768] for d in docs]
scores = cosine_similarity(query_trunc, docs_trunc)
# scores distribution shows many high outliers vs full-dim similarity
```

alex_support: Two asks: (1) for the customer, what's a short-term mitigation? (2) for engineering, what's the fix plan?

kevin-ml: Mitigation: recompute embeddings with the rerank model's recommended embedder (emb-small-compat) or call the /v1/embeddings endpoint with model=emb-small-compat for those docs. If recomputing is slow, another short-term hack is to up/down-project vectors with our transform endpoint (not ideal). Example curl to recompute: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"emb-small-compat","input":["doc text 1","doc text 2"]}'
```

jon-platform: For fix: I propose we change compatibility_mode default back to strict: reject any precomputed embeddings whose dim != model_expected_dim with 400 + helpful message. And add an optional query param allow_compat=true to opt into legacy pad/truncate. That keeps safety while preserving backward compat for clients who relied on the old behavior.

kevin-ml: Agreed. Also add a server-side warning in logs when truncation/padding happens and surface a deprecation notice in the API docs. We'll add a validation check: if incoming_dim != expected_dim -> 400 unless allow_compat=true. Tests: unit tests for both paths + integration test comparing scores between recomputed and truncated flows.

alex_support: For this customer, I told them to recompute embeddings with emb-small-compat and re-run rerank. I'll provide a small migration script.

acme-cs: Appreciate the quick analysis. We'll start recomputing and patching our pipeline. A couple questions: (1) timeline for the strict validation rollout? (2) any chance to get a temporary flag to enable full-dim projection on your side while we migrate?

kevin-ml: Timeline: plan to push the validation + docs change today to canary, monitor for 2 hours, then production deploy in next maintenance window (~6h). For temporary flag: we can enable allow_compat=true for your API key as a short-term setting — ops, can you handle that, @jon-platform?

jon-platform: Yes, I can flip allow_compat for api_key: ak_live_acme for 48h. I'll also add a rate-limited deprecation banner for that key.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rerank-validation-canary @kevin-ml
deploy-bot: Canary deployed to 10% of traffic at 1715004625
deploy-bot: Canary report: no errors, latency +1.2%, validation triggered for ~0.3% of requests (mostly internal).

kevin-ml: Canary looks clean. Rolling to prod now.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete at 1715004760. Validation mode: strict by default. allow_compat flag available per-key.

acme-cs: Confirmed: after recomputing with emb-small-compat our rerank ordering looks correct again. Thanks all :raised_hands:

alex_support: I'll follow up with a short thread for KB + customer migration script and close this thread once docs are posted.

kevin-ml: Filed follow-up PRs: docs+deprecation notice and an infra task to remove allow_compat default in 90 days.

acme-cs: Great, thanks for the rapid help.
